# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel an embossed warning that says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” No wire properties are apparent to touch, so I need the manual’s rule and the Deaf monkey’s visual observations before taking any action. I will tell Mute the tactile warning and ask for the relevant instructions, while signaling Deaf that I have no wire information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel an embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I cannot distinguish anything about wires 1, 2, or 3 by touch. Tell me the manual rule and what action is permitted.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display reads 0. Light is red. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Blind just gestured thumbs down; meaning unknown.

The Deaf monkey reports that the display is 0, the light is red, and wires 1–3 are green, yellow, and blue respectively. The embossed warning confirms that no wire should be cut. I still need the manual’s instructions, so I will pass along all observed information to Mute and request the rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, red light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. The embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. What does the manual instruct us to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured thumbs up, then pointing upward. I do not know what this means. Bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The bomb’s state is unchanged, and the warning still forbids cutting any wire. Deaf reports that Mute made a thumbs-up followed by an upward-pointing gesture, but that signal has no established meaning for me. I will ask Mute to state the manual’s instruction in words rather than gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual instruction explicitly in words. Do not rely on gestures; I cannot see them.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again gestured thumbs up, then pointing upward. This repeated signal is still of unknown meaning.

Mute cannot answer aloud, so the repeated gestures are likely an attempted response that has not been decoded. I will establish a simple wire-number code: one raised finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, and thumbs-down for “cut none.” I will ask Mute to use that exact gesture and ask Deaf to report it literally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use gestures to answer. Gesture exactly one symbol: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, and 👎 means cut no wire. Do not use thumbs up or pointing upward.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured folded hands, then pointing upward, then palm facing downward. Interpret this using the manual if possible.

The repeated hand sequence is still not a reliable instruction: I can only know that Mute made three gestures, not what the manual says they mean. The only direct tactile instruction remains “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and no safe cut has been identified. I will ask Mute to use the agreed single-symbol code once more, with no extra gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret three gestures. Please make exactly one gesture: 👎 means cut no wire; ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestured pointing upward only: ?. Bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

Mute has now made one upward-pointing gesture, which under the code I proposed would mean wire 1—but the Deaf monkey’s report does not establish that Mute intended our code. More importantly, the tactile warning explicitly says not to cut any wire, so I will not risk acting on an ambiguous signal. I will ask Mute to confirm “cut none” with the agreed thumbs-down gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. If the manual says to cut none, gesture exactly 👎 and nothing else. Otherwise use one of the agreed wire symbols.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent only pointing upward: ?. This is now repeated. Bomb still shows 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Mute has repeatedly sent the single upward-pointing gesture, matching the agreed code for wire 1. Although the tactile warning is concerning, Mute’s manual-based signal is the only available operational instruction, and its repetition indicates confirmation. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
